cohort: The study participants were women identified from 7,916,388 births recorded in the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample from 2003 to 2011.
finding: The incidence of Hodgkin's lymphoma in pregnancy was higher than previously reported, and while associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, postpartum blood transfusion, and venous thromboembolism, overall maternal and neonatal major morbidity and mortality did not appear to be increased.
